← E-Bike Rental Fleet Profit Calculator

How much does an e-bike rental business make?

Twenty bikes open 180 days a season rent about 3600 half-day slots. At that level the shop keeps about a fifth of its revenue and the start-up money comes back in under two years. Here is the arithmetic, line by line.

The worked example

A shop with 20 bikes has 40 half-day slots a day. It is open 100 busy days at 70% utilization and 80 quiet days at 25%, so it rents 3600 of 7200 slots, 50.0% of capacity. Half days sell at $40 and full days at $65, and 45% of rented slots are full days, a blended $36.63 per slot. The 2790 rentals add $6 each in add-ons, $16,740, for $148,590 of revenue.

Staff is 2 people for 9 hours on each of 180 days at $17 an hour plus 12% extras, $61,690. Rent, insurance, marketing and other fixed costs are $28,500. Damage and theft (3%) and card fees (3%) take $8,915, tires, brakes and charging $6,480 and batteries $2,591.

The fleet must be replaced eventually, so the calculator sets aside $9,533 a season: 20 bikes at $2,200, less 35% resale, over 3 seasons. Total costs are $117,709 and the season profit is $30,881, a margin of 20.8%, or $1,544 per bike.

Start-up cost is $56,000 (the bikes plus $12,000 of racks, locks and chargers), a payback of 1.8 years. The shop breaks even at 38.2% utilization, and a 20% margin needs prices of $39.52 for a half day and $64.23 for a full day.

What if bookings fall short

With 10% fewer bookings the season profit falls to $17,821, and with 20% fewer it is $4,760. Staff and rent do not move, so a bad summer removes profit much faster than it removes revenue.

What a bigger fleet changes

Growing to 30 bikes while utilization slips to 62% on busy days and 22% on quiet days lifts the season profit to $68,778 and shortens the payback to 1.1 years, but profit per bike falls to $2,293. Each added bike earns less than the first ones, which is why the utilization you enter for the bigger fleet matters more than the number of bikes.

Common questions

How many days a year does an e-bike rental shop need to be busy?

The calculator does not assume a number: enter your busy and quiet days and their utilization, and it solves the overall utilization at which the season breaks even. Staff and rent are paid on every open day, so a long quiet shoulder season can cost more than it earns.

Is it better to rent by the half day or the full day?

A full day uses two half-day slots, so a full-day price below twice the half-day price discounts the bike's time. The calculator blends both using the share of full days you expect, and keeps your price ratio when it solves the lowest prices.

When does buying more e-bikes stop paying?

When the extra bikes are rented on fewer days than the first ones. Enter the bigger fleet and the lower utilization you honestly expect in scenario B and compare total profit, profit per bike and payback.

Run your own numbers in the calculator.

E-BIKE RENTAL FLEET PROFIT CALCULATOR · RUNS IN YOUR BROWSER · NOTHING UPLOADED

Will an e-bike rental fleet pay for itself?

Enter your bikes, how many busy and quiet days you open and how full the fleet gets, your half-day and full-day prices, and your staff, rent, batteries and loan. See season profit, payback, the utilization you need to break even, the lowest prices that hit your margin, and what a bigger fleet would change.

For bike shops, hotels, campgrounds and tour desks adding or growing an e-bike rental counter. No sign-up. New to this? Read how much an e-bike rental business makes, with a worked example.

Scenario A is the numbers above. Change only what differs: for example a bigger fleet with the lower utilization you expect, or different prices.

How it works

Slots. Each bike has two half-day slots a day. A full-day rental uses both. Utilization is the share of slots rented, set separately for busy and quiet days. Revenue is rented slots times the blended price per slot, plus add-ons per rental.

Costs are damage and theft and card fees as a share of revenue, staff for every open day, rent, insurance, marketing, wear and charging per rented slot, batteries per rental, and a fleet replacement reserve: bike cost less resale, spread over the seasons you keep it. Payback is start-up cost divided by yearly operating profit after that reserve, before the loan.

Break-even and the lowest prices are solved exactly, because operating profit is a straight line in utilization and in the price level, then checked by typing them back in. Not included: taxes, claims and deductibles, weather risk beyond the utilization you choose, and growth in later seasons.

Common questions

How much does an e-bike rental business make?

It depends on the size of the fleet, how many days you are open and how many of your bikes are out on those days. The calculator turns your bikes, busy and quiet days, utilization, prices, staff, rent and other costs into profit for a season, so you can see which assumption the answer depends on.

What utilization does an e-bike rental shop need to break even?

The calculator solves it exactly from your own costs: the share of half-day slots that must be rented, over the whole season, for profit after any loan payments to reach zero. Staff and rent do not fall when fewer bikes go out, so break-even is often higher than owners expect.

How many e-bikes should I buy?

Add bikes in scenario B and enter the utilization you honestly expect with the bigger fleet. Each added bike costs money but is rented fewer days than the first ones, so compare total profit, profit per bike and payback side by side before you buy.

How much should I charge for an e-bike rental?

The calculator solves the lowest half-day and full-day prices, keeping your price ratio, that break even, reach your target margin and meet your payback target at the utilization you entered. Compare them with what other local renters charge before you set prices.

Does this include the cost of replacing the bikes?

Yes, as a yearly fleet replacement reserve: the bike cost less what you expect to sell it for, spread over the seasons you keep it. Batteries are charged per rental, and tires, brakes and charging per rented slot.

Does this include insurance claims, permits or sales tax?

Only the yearly insurance and other costs you type. It does not model liability claims, deductibles, permits, licences, sales or income tax. Check those with your insurer, your city and a tax professional.

Is my data uploaded anywhere?

No. Everything is calculated in your browser from what you type, nothing is sent to a server, there are no accounts, and you can save the analysis to a file on your own device.
